pezzi.36: Something new comes out every week. I read the benchmarks again instead of inheriting last year’s choice: intelligence index, cost per task, coding agents index.
pezzi.38: Artificial Analysis publishes independent indices. The intelligence index is a composite: nine weighted evaluations, not a single exam. The version matters, because the numbers from one version to the next are not comparable.
pezzi.42: GDPval-AA v2, τ³-Banking, Terminal-Bench v2.1, SciCode, HLE, GPQA Diamond, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR
pezzi.48: In red, the models I use or am weighing up for client work. Next to the score, the index’s average cost per task: two numbers to be read together, never one alone.
pezzi.68: Every dot is a model. Bottom left, you spend little and get little. Top right, you get a lot and spend a lot. The dashed line joins the models that, at that cost, nobody beats: that is where the choice is made.
pezzi.89: , Intelligence Index v4.1.1 and average cost per task · read on 21 August 2026 · logarithmic horizontal scale
pezzi.91: A separate index: it does not measure the model on its own, it measures the agent plus model pair on software engineering tasks carried through to the end. It is the measure that counts when an agent works inside a repository.
pezzi.109: , coding agents index v1.4 · 14 rows out of the 55 in the ranking · read on 21 August 2026 ·
pezzi.112: Three tests with equal weights, each with its own number of tasks. Every task is attempted three times, and what counts is how often it succeeds on the first try: one lucky attempt is not enough.
pezzi.120: In the ranking the top ten sit within 6,5 points: the distance between first and tenth is smaller than the price suggests
pezzi.121: The number that decides the quote
pezzi.122: Between first and fourth place there’s a gap of two and a half points of index and, vis-à-vis the leader, less than half the cost per task.
pezzi.124: The list price is not the cost: it changes with the cache, with the length of the context and with reasoning tokens. These are the items to look at separately.
pezzi.135: The cache is not a detail
pezzi.136: On an agent that rereads the same instructions at every step, the cache decides the bill. The rules change from provider to provider and have to be read before choosing.
pezzi.138: A tenth of an input token’s price (Anthropic)
pezzi.140: A quarter more than an input token’s price
pezzi.144: A badly written agent pays for the cache on writes and never uses it on reads
pezzi.146: There is no best model. There is the right model for that step, and the choice is made again when the numbers move.
pezzi.148: Steps that decide: planning, verification, review

pezzi.154: Data that must not leave the machine
pezzi.156: These numbers have a date: they are the photograph of 21 August 2026. A ranking read six months from now says something else, and anyone quoting it without a date is selling an old decision. The values sit in a single file next to the site, and an automatic check compares the page against that file: if the two drift apart, the check turns red and the page is not published.
